cohort: 498 newborns born at 34+0 to 36+6 weeks of gestational age, without major malformations, chromosomopathies, hydrops fetalis, or congenital TORCH infection
finding: Late preterm infants, particularly those delivered after 35 weeks by cesarean section, remain at risk for adverse respiratory outcomes, highlighting the need for strategies to reduce cesarean section rates and improve respiratory care in this population.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was an independent risk factor for respiratory morbidity in late preterm infants.
